integrity: For adjacent endpoints u and v, triangle inequality forces the two distances from any vertex w to differ by at most one. Unequal distances are therefore equivalent to a difference of exactly one, which is equivalent to one endpoint lying on a geodesic from w to the other. Thus the two neighborhoods coincide edge by edge, making the two feasible polytopes identical. An exhaustive checker independently confirms neighborhood equality for all 27,475 connected labeled graphs on at most six vertices.
scientific_limitations: The equivalence is for the published local-strong definition restricted to adjacent vertex pairs.
Ordinary fractional metric dimension and fractional strong metric dimension for arbitrary vertex pairs do not follow from this argument.
The exhaustive graph enumeration through six vertices is corroborative only; the universal theorem follows directly from the distance identity for adjacent endpoints.
A differently named or non-indexed source could have observed the same equivalence despite targeted searches.
title: Local fractional strong metric dimension collapses to local fractional metric dimension
